title: Chapter 20: Crime Scene
html:
A mysterious fire, an unsolved case, and a missing culprit—Chen Ge discovered that he had a knack for storytelling. He condensed the old reports, mixed in his own theories, and turned the building’s history into a compelling mystery for his audience.

“That’s the background. I came here looking for inspiration for my Haunted House, but I discovered something strange: every tenant I’ve met seems to be hiding something. I suspect whoever was responsible for the old case may still be connected to this building.” Chen Ge looked directly into the camera.

“Interesting. So it’s a real-life mystery? Anyone have a brilliant theory?”

I’m a Little Green Worm mocked him. “Host, you’re good at making things sound dramatic, but we’re not that gullible!”

“I just searched Fu An Apartments in Jiujiang. The old case is real, at least.”

He San offered some support. “I believe the host.”

I’m a Little Green Worm remained unconvinced. “Even if the case is real, how do we know he’s actually there? He said the building was damaged by a fire, but look at his room. The walls are painted and the furniture is usable, if old. Does that look like an abandoned crime scene to you?”

“You want proof? Fine.” Chen Ge moved the makeup table aside and picked at a loose edge of paint near the wall. “A building can be renamed, renovated, and repainted, but old damage is harder to erase completely.”

Beneath the newer surface was older, smoke-darkened masonry. “This building really was affected by that fire.”

“Forget the wall. Why did you come prepared like you expected trouble?” Death to All Men asked.

“Host is damaging the landlord’s wall for content. One minute of silence for the security deposit.”

“How much did you pay for this room? It doesn’t even have a television.”

Reading the chat, Chen Ge sighed. “Could you people focus? I’m spending the night in a supposedly haunted apartment for this stream, and all you care about is the wallpaper?”

Death to All Men sent a small donation. “There. Respect shown.”

Chen Ge had no idea how to deal with the trolls, but at least they were staying. “Fine. Back to the mystery. I’ve met six people since I arrived. The first was a woman on the first floor. She smiled at me in a way I couldn’t read, but I haven’t spoken to her since, so I don’t know much about her.”

He introduced the rest of the tenants and then added his own analysis. “In terms of opportunity, the landlord is suspicious because he controls the building, but his limp limits his mobility. The tattooed man on the first floor and the heavyset man on the second floor are physically more capable. Then there’s Wang Qi, whose story doesn’t quite add up, and the woman downstairs, whom I know almost nothing about.”

“So basically, you’ve learned nothing,” Death to All Men summarized. “By your logic, even the old man could be hiding something. He inherited the property, didn’t he?”

“It isn’t impossible that he knows more than he appears to,” another viewer replied. “Whatever his condition is now, we don’t know what he was like years ago.”

“Exactly. Everyone’s circumstances could have changed since the fire. You can’t rule someone out based only on how they look today.”

“I’m still suspicious of the woman downstairs,” another viewer wrote. “That smile sounded deliberate. Host, do you remember anything else about her expression or body language?”

“Not really…”

As the viewers became more invested, the stream’s popularity rose with them. Watching the chat fly past, Chen Ge sighed inwardly.These people are hopeless. I’ll have to find more clues myself before any of this makes sense.

He propped the phone in front of him. “I looked around the building before starting the stream. Most of the first and second floors have been repaired, but part of the third floor was left almost untouched after the old fire. I’m going up there to take a closer look. Maybe we’ll find something useful.”

“They left part of it untouched for years? That’s creepy.”

“Maybe that’s why all the ghost stories started.”

“Exploring a supposedly haunted apartment at night? This host is committed, I’ll give him that.”

“He runs a Haunted House! A bunch of us went there after his last scary video. Two of the bravest entered first—one came out in tears and the other fainted.”

“What happened to the rest of you?”

“What do you think? After seeing that, none of us went in!”

“Fair point.”

“LOL!” He San commented.

The chat had completely derailed, but Chen Ge did not mind. Holding his phone, he headed for the door.

Remembering his earlier scare, he paused and listened carefully before easing the door open.

After locking the room behind him, Chen Ge left a subtle marker that would tell him if the door had been disturbed while he was gone.

With that done, he headed toward the stairwell.

He moved quietly, using the light from his phone to guide him. As he climbed, the walls grew progressively darker, and a stale, unpleasant odor thickened in the air.

When he reached the third floor, he turned on his phone’s flashlight and paused to listen.

The first time he had wandered up here, he had seen a dark shape dart across the corridor. For an instant, it had looked almost human.

Ghost or human, I need to be careful.The flashlight swept across the part of the building that had been left untouched for years. Deep marks scored the walls, and the corridor seemed even more oppressive than he remembered.

Ping An Apartments had an unusual layout. A single stairwell occupied the right side of the building, making the corridor stretching left feel unnaturally long.

As Chen Ge advanced, a chill crawled up his spine. Even with one shoulder near the wall, he felt strangely exposed.

If the worst of the fire started elsewhere, that would explain why so much of the third floor survived. Maybe whoever caused it never needed to come up here.

He continued along the dark corridor. Doors on both sides had warped with age and heat, opening onto blackened, abandoned rooms.

Picking his way around the rubbish on the floor, Chen Ge slipped into the nearest room he could enter.
